Shahazimah
shah-huh-ZYE-mah
proper noun
Hebrew Shachatsimah, perhaps “heights” or “lofty places”; a town of Issachar near Tabor, on the border reaching to Jordan.

📖 Biblical Definition

Shahazimah was a town of Issachar, named as the tribal coast ran toward Tabor and the Jordan: “And the coast reacheth to Tabor, and Shahazimah, and Bethshemesh; and the outgoings of their border were at Jordan” (Josh 19:22). Issachar lay in the good and pleasant vale of Jezreel, between the hills of Galilee and the ridge of Carmel, a fertile plain that made the tribe a willing labourer. Jacob had seen it: “Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens: and he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear” (Gen 49:14-15). Shahazimah, if its name means “heights,” stood among the swelling grounds of that rich plain. The tribe of the strong ass preaches the dignity of patient labour and the danger of ease. Issachar bore his burden willingly, and Moses blessed him to rejoice in his tents; yet the love of ease that bowed the shoulder to tribute could sink into servility if rest were prized above righteousness. The believer learns to labour gladly and bear his burden, taking the yoke of Christ, which is easy, and finding rest not in the pleasantness of the land but in the God who gives His beloved rest.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Issachar near Tabor (Josh 19:22); a town of the tribe of the strong ass, preaching the dignity of patient labour and the danger of ease.

SHAHAZIMAH, a town of Issachar near Tabor.

Named as the coast reached to Jordan (Josh 19:22).

The name may mean “heights” or “lofty places.”

Issachar lay in the pleasant vale of Jezreel.

A town of the strong ass, dignity of labour and danger of ease.

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 19:22 — "And the coast reacheth to Tabor, and Shahazimah, and Bethshemesh; and the outgoings of their border were at Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages."

Gen 49:14 — "Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens:"

Gen 49:15 — "And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute."

Josh 19:23 — "This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities and their villages."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A town of Issachar near Tabor; it recovers the dignity of patient labour and the danger of prizing ease above righteousness.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A town named once raises no modern quarrel. It lay in Issachar’s pleasant plain, the tribe Jacob likened to a strong ass bowing to bear its burden.

The principle to recover is the dignity of patient labour and the danger of ease. Issachar bore his burden willingly and rejoiced in his tents, yet the love of pleasant rest could sink into servility if ease were prized above righteousness. The believer labours gladly, takes the easy yoke of Christ, and seeks rest not in the pleasantness of the land but in the God who gives His beloved rest.
